title: Animate the opening Milky Way view with pinned YEIS native auto-orbit

scope.subject: Use the pinned MIT YEIS CameraController autoOrbit capability for a subtle opening-galaxy drift without creating a second camera animation authority

research_summary: The pinned MIT YEIS CameraController already implements slow automatic orbit around an active orbit pivot, explicitly intended for opening backdrops and guided-tour dwell. It automatically cancels on mouse, wheel, touch or keyboard input. The product should activate that native field only on a fresh galaxy view, while preserving the existing controller as the sole camera authority and disabling motion for reduced-motion users and deterministic ?freeze=1 validation.

sources.finding: Pinned MIT YEIS CameraController exposes autoOrbit specifically for slow opening-view/tour rotation and cancels it immediately when the visitor takes control.
The existing R3F frame loop already drives the selected YEIS CameraController, so no second RAF loop or camera system is needed.

search_ladder.conclusion: Reuse the selected pinned MIT YEIS camera system rather than adding another animation/camera library.
Keep the existing R3F frame loop; the native controller already updates inside it.
Activate CameraController.autoOrbit on the fresh Milky Way orbit anchor and let its built-in input takeover semantics stop the drift.
No new component or animation asset is required.

candidates.name: Pinned MIT YEIS CameraController.autoOrbit
candidates.reason: Already owns the galaxy camera, explicitly supports opening-view drift, and automatically yields to visitor input.

candidates.name: Custom R3F useFrame quaternion/orbit drift
candidates.reason: Would duplicate behavior already present in the selected YEIS camera authority and risks fighting manual input/autopilot.

candidates.name: CSS transform on WebGL canvas
candidates.reason: Moves presentation without moving the spatial camera, so picking, labels and navigation geometry would diverge from what the visitor sees.

coverage_matrix.decision: Use native autoOrbit at a subtle rate.
Reuse CameraController's existing automatic cancellation on pointer, wheel, touch and keyboard input.
Do not add a parallel animation loop or DOM transform.

decision.rationale: Activate the pinned MIT YEIS autoOrbit field only for a fresh opening Milky Way view. Keep CameraController as sole spatial authority, stop automatically on visitor control, and suppress the motion for reduced-motion/frozen validation.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: R3F can implement the same motion, but doing so would recreate controller behavior that YEIS already supplies and complicate takeover/autopilot ownership.

decision.fallback: If opening auto-orbit harms interaction or composition, set the activation speed to zero and retain the existing static YEIS opening view; do not introduce another camera animation system.
